reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any real normed vector space. Fix any function g:E->E, any real eta and epsilon, any anchor y in E, and any starting point x in E. Let n,m be natural numbers and let r,s be pairs in E x N. Suppose
  run(g,eta,epsilon,y,n,x)=some(r),
  run(g,eta,epsilon,y,m,x)=some(s).
Then r=s: both the returned point and the actual reported evaluation count are identical.
The finite exact-real interpreter returns none when its fuel is zero. With positive fuel, it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), and returns (x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. Otherwise it recurses from next with fuel reduced by one, adding one to a successful returned count. The count includes the final successful evaluation. The theorem says that any two successful executions with the same g,eta,epsilon,y,x agree regardless of their possibly different fuel budgets. It imposes no positivity condition on eta or epsilon, no continuity or measurability condition on g, and no inner-product, completeness, finite-dimensionality, or probability-space assumptions. It asserts neither that an execution succeeds nor that n=m; surplus fuel may differ while the successful returned pair agrees.
objects: A real normed space E; arbitrary map g:E->E; real parameters eta,epsilon; fixed anchor y and initial iterate x; natural fuel budgets n,m; two successful output/count pairs r,s in E x N; and the exact-real finite interpreter run.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup and NormedSpace R structures. g:E->E, eta/epsilon in R, x/y in E, n/m in N, and r/s in E x N. run has an optional pair output, failing with none or succeeding with some(point,count). No measure, random law, finite index set, inner-product structure, completeness or finite-dimensionality is present.
quantifiers: For every real normed space E, every g,eta,epsilon,y,x, every natural n,m and every pair r,s: if both executions with their respective fuel budgets and the identical other inputs return those successful pairs, then r=s. All quantities are universally quantified conditional inputs. There is no existentially quantified successful run or witness.
assumptions: Only the real normed-space structures and the two exact successful-run equalities are assumed. The same function, parameters, anchor and initial point are used by both runs. eta and epsilon are unrestricted real numbers and g is an unrestricted function. There are no convergence, contraction, smoothness, positivity, probability, continuity or measurability assumptions.
conclusion: r=s as pairs in E x N, so both successful executions return the same E-valued point and the same natural-valued actual evaluation count, including the terminal successful evaluation. Equality of the fuel budgets is not concluded.
scopes: The identity is conditional on both executions succeeding and compares arbitrary finite fuel budgets for one fixed deterministic input tuple. The count is the reported actual number of evaluations, not the supplied fuel. This does not assert eventual termination, existence of a successful fuel budget, equality of budgets, solution accuracy, convergence, or any probabilistic complexity estimate.
constant_dependencies: No quantitative constants or bounds occur. Equality requires the same E,g,eta,epsilon,y,x in both executions. n,m may differ; the conclusion identifies their successful return values without dependence on a particular adequate fuel budget. The interpreter stopping threshold is (1-eta)epsilon, with no positivity assumption.
